drafted_from: tool:github:yt-dlp-yt-dlp's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic names filled in. What it prints or writes is read from the tool's documented behavior; the folder test test/index-github-tools.test.mjs only checks the row, never runs yt-dlp.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use yt-dlp on my computer to download a video or its audio from a web address such as YouTube: the file is https://example.com/watch?v=demo123." It reads the row, installs yt-dlp if it is missing, runs it on that one file and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: yt-dlp is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on the one file or address it is handed.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use yt-dlp on https://example.com/watch?v=demo123". It reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:yt-dlp-yt-dlp"}.

2. It checks that python, ffmpeg are on your computer, and if yt-dlp is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp.git ; python -m pip install -U --pre "yt-dlp[default]".
3. It runs the row's command with your file in place of {input}: yt-dlp https://example.com/watch?v=demo123
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. Trillion runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: yt-dlp on a public video page at example.com
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:yt-dlp-yt-dlp runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got yt-dlp in, the command line: yt-dlp https://example.com/watch?v=demo123  (synthetic input: a public video page at example.com).
worked_examples.hands_back: yt-dlp prints the lines it downloads by ("[download] Destination: ..."), then "[download] 100% of 12.40MiB", and leaves the video file in the folder it ran in, named with the video's title and id.
